reference.source: Bradley's Neurology in Clinical Practice / Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
clinicalPearls: An autosomal recessive leukodystrophy caused by mutations in the ASPA gene resulting in deficiency of aspartoacylase
Enzyme deficiency leads to accumulation of N-acetylaspartate, which is measurably elevated in urine and can be detected as a raised NAA peak on MR spectroscopy
Classic infantile disease presents in the first months with hypotonia, poor head control, macrocephaly, and progressive developmental failure
As disease progresses, hypotonia often gives way to spasticity, with seizures, feeding difficulties, and optic atrophy
It is one of the leukodystrophies with increased carrier frequency in the Ashkenazi Jewish population, making carrier screening relevant in that group
MRI shows diffuse, symmetric white matter disease, and elevated N-acetylaspartate on spectroscopy strongly supports the diagnosis
Diagnosis is confirmed by demonstrating elevated urinary N-acetylaspartate and by ASPA gene testing
Macrocephaly in an infant with developmental regression should raise suspicion and prompt appropriate metabolic and imaging workup
reference.pathophysiology: Canavan disease arises from biallelic ASPA mutations causing deficiency of aspartoacylase, the enzyme that hydrolyses N-acetylaspartate in the brain. The resulting accumulation of N-acetylaspartate is thought to disturb myelin maintenance and fluid balance, producing spongy vacuolar degeneration of white matter. The intramyelinic oedema and dysmyelination give the characteristic diffuse leukodystrophy and clinical picture of progressive neurological failure with macrocephaly.
additionalDifferentials: Other infantile leukodystrophies including Alexander disease
Other causes of macrocephaly with developmental regression
additionalInvestigations: ASPA gene sequencing to confirm the diagnosis
Brain MRI showing diffuse symmetric white matter change
MR spectroscopy demonstrating an elevated N-acetylaspartate peak
Carrier screening and genetic counselling for at-risk families
Developmental and feeding assessments for supportive care
redFlags: Progressive loss of milestones with seizures in an infant
Feeding and swallowing failure risking aspiration and malnutrition
reference.prognosis: Classic infantile Canavan disease is progressive with limited life expectancy and no curative therapy, so care is supportive; milder variants with later onset follow a more variable and slower course.
pitfalls: Attributing macrocephaly to benign causes without considering a leukodystrophy
Overlooking the diagnostic value of urinary N-acetylaspartate and MR spectroscopy
Failing to offer carrier screening and counselling in high-risk populations
Delaying supportive measures for feeding and seizures
management: Provide supportive care as the mainstay, since no curative or disease-specific therapy is established
Reduce spasticity with antispasticity agents such as baclofen alongside physiotherapy and positioning
Support nutrition and manage feeding difficulties, with gastrostomy feeding where swallowing is unsafe
Manage secretions and provide respiratory care as neurological function declines
Offer genetic counselling and carrier screening, particularly for families of Ashkenazi Jewish origin, with prenatal testing options
Coordinate multidisciplinary and palliative support across neurology, therapy services and the family
